headline: Pin the boards you live in, on a landing that sits flat
summary: A pinned board is exempt from the recent history's 24-slot cap, so the two or three boards you actually work in stop scrolling away. The landing is redrawn on the board canvas's own grid — flat, with the banding, the popping and the seam across the middle gone.

new.title: Pin a board so the history stops evicting it
new.description: Recents are a history capped at 24 — opening a board puts it at the front and the tail falls off. That is right for a history and wrong for the two or three boards you live in, which scroll off after a busy week with nothing you can do about it. A pinned board is exempt, and pins are kept in addition to the recent slots rather than competing for them, so pinning something never costs you a slot in your history. Pins lead the landing in both layouts and the card stays marked whether or not a pointer is near it. Twelve pins maximum — past that the landing says so rather than silently dropping the oldest, and an entry that loses its pin is demoted to an ordinary recent rather than discarded.

improved.title: The landing is drawn on the board canvas's own grid
improved.description: The landing now carries the same surface the work happens on: one line per 48 pixels at a tenth of the accent's strength, so it reads as structure rather than decoration, with the light and the lines falling off together from the top. The two drifting aurora fields it replaces left a visible seam across the middle of the page where their falloffs crossed — a single masked layer has nothing to cross. A hairline closes the header in Focus Flow, and the card row dissolves into the background at both edges instead of being cut off by the window.

improved.title: The restore prompt is a pill instead of a banner
improved.description: The prompt offering to reopen your last board was a 1120 by 71 pixel banner asking a single question, wide enough to crowd the card beneath it. It is a 577 by 50 pixel pill now, centred and on one line, and the flush-left accent bar — which stood proud of the rounded edge and read as a rendering fault — is an inline dot.

improved.title: Dock chips stay chip-sized however few boards you have
improved.description: The chips under the carousel split whatever width the row gave them, with no upper limit. At the 24 board cap that lands around 18 pixels and looks right; at three boards it was 170 pixels each, and at one board a single 520 pixel slab lit bright blue — a segmented progress bar, the exact thing the dock replaced. A 22 pixel cap and a centred row keep every count inside one narrow band, so the dock reads the same whether you have two boards or two dozen.

fixed.title: The carousel no longer paints over the classic grid
fixed.description: Switching to Classic Grid hid the carousel by attribute, but a display rule added with the footer work outranked what that attribute asks for, so the renderer ignored it and the whole carousel — fourteen cards, both arrows, the hint and the dock — kept painting on top of the grid. Each layout now shows only its own content.

fixed.title: Cards no longer pop as the pointer moves along the row
fixed.description: A card's resting background is a gradient, and the hover rule replaced it with a flat colour — which no browser can interpolate, so the quarter-second transition sitting right there in the rule was ignored and the card snapped instead. Scrolling with the pointer over the row hands hover from card to card on every step, firing that snap over and over. Hover is now a gradient of the same shape, so only the colours differ and the fade actually runs.

fixed.title: Card buttons no longer flash while the carousel moves
fixed.description: Cards slide under a stationary cursor, so each one passing briefly counted as hovered and faded its three buttons in while the previous card's faded out — sampled mid-scroll, the number of buttons on screen flipped between three and six. The buttons are held back until the row settles now, and return on the card under the cursor once it stops.

fixed.title: The banding across the carousel is gone
fixed.description: Two things printed hard horizontal edges onto the flattened page, and neither was a gradient. The receding cards were dimmed but barely faded — the furthest still sat at 84 percent opacity — so they met the page as solid slabs; the depth ramp now comes out of the opacity as well, and a card two back is a suggestion rather than a shape. And 96 pixels of shadow blur at low alpha over a near-black page steps visibly, showing as arcs around each card: the widest glow is gone, the drops are shorter, and the film grain sits above the cards now, where it can dither them.

fixed.title: The landing backdrop is identical in both layouts
fixed.description: The grain blends with whatever is behind it and only Focus Flow isolated it, so in Classic Grid it came out a different texture. The grid and the grain were also positioned inside the scrolling container, so in Classic they slid away with the content, and the scrollbar narrowed their box by its own width and moved every line about five pixels. Both layers are fixed to the viewport now — same geometry in both layouts, and they stay put while the grid scrolls under them.

fixed.title: A search that finds nothing clears the dock and the counter
fixed.description: The no-result path emptied the cards, but the dock and the position counter live outside the track and were left describing boards that were no longer on screen — nine chips for a carousel with nothing in it, and a counter still reading 1 of 9. It sat hidden behind the empty state, so nothing showed it, and it healed itself on the next search that matched. Both are cleared properly now.
